title: Restore Jobs that never start hang the restore with Kanidm at zero replicas

source.reference: kaniop v0.24.1 live backup/restore review (B3, B4; findings F3A.6, F4A.6, F3B.11). A safety repository with a missing client-side KEK Secret quiesced Kanidm and the safety Job stayed in CreateContainerConfigError forever; a safetyBackup.repositoryRef to a missing repository stayed in Validating forever with an empty message and blocked other restores. Restore Jobs had no scheduling inheritance and no activeDeadlineSeconds, and job_state ignored the Job Failed condition, so after databaseMutationStarted no phase could reach Failed and force-release was impossible.

required_properties: The restore controller treats a Job with condition Failed=True (for example reason DeadlineExceeded) as failed even when status.failed is zero, with a unit test that fails on the v0.24.1 job_state
Every restore Job (safety backup, source preparation, source check, restore, verify) sets activeDeadlineSeconds so a Job that cannot start or finish fails instead of holding the target quiesced
Restore Jobs copy nodeSelector, tolerations and only affinity.nodeAffinity from the primary replica group; podAffinity, podAntiAffinity and topologySpreadConstraints are not copied
A Job failure before the mutation boundary resumes the target; after it the restore reaches phase Failed so the force-release annotation can release the lock
Validating fails the restore with a message naming the repository when the safety repository does not exist, instead of returning the 404 outside validation

Validating requires Ready/Accepted for the source and safety repositories and, when a repository references a KEK, EncryptionKeyReady=True plus a direct check that the KEK Secret exists and contains the key
Every validation failure leaves databaseMutationStarted=false, no maintenance annotation, the original replica counts, and no restore Job
Creating a safety repository together with a restore keeps working: a repository whose status has not been reported yet waits in Validating rather than failing
forbidden_changes: Copy the full affinity (pod affinity or anti-affinity) or topologySpreadConstraints into restore Jobs
Treat FailureTarget alone as failed, which could resume Kanidm while a Job pod still holds the primary PVC
Change the CRD or hand-edit charts/kaniop/crds/crds.yaml or files under examples/
Weaken the mutation boundary, the fail-closed post-mutation lock, or the force-release requirement
Add a controller-side phase timer instead of using the Job activeDeadlineSeconds
Fail every restore whose safety repository has not been reconciled yet
